doc.title: Ken Peplowski interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 9, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Bill Maher, lockdowns and wearing masks
summary: He disagrees with Maher's Sweden-style view, arguing lockdowns prevented far more deaths, and says people should wear masks.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: and a similar number of deaths. And then he said, you know, “People, the statistics of people that die of infections in hospitals is also a hundred thousand a year and nobody talks about that.” But what I would argue about that is we’ve had a hundred thousand deaths because we did the lockdown, and if we hadn’t we might be at five hundred thousand you know? So I think this pandemic is probably worse than any we’ve ever seen. And as painful as it is for all of us I think it’s something we have to do. You know here in New York, and maybe it’s the same where you are, so many people are walking around outside just hanging around in groups and no masks, nothing. And I don’t understand that. Because it doesn’t kill you to wear that mask. And every epidemiologist, nobody disagrees on that, it’s not even a thing that’s debated yet, you know, everybody is saying you still should wear them when you’re outside to protect yourself and to protect other people.
